claim: FILO Circular Buffer RMS: the window becomes 'time they can hear' — 500 samples is 11 ms, 1000 sluggish, 100 twitchy; and Soft Knee Mathematics: a sharp knee is broadband while the quadratic knee has bounded Fourier content.

pieces.what: The buffer drawn as a ring of samples filling and emptying, with a window slider (100, 500, 1000) on one drum loop; the reader hears sluggish and twitchy. (The buffer adds the newest and drops the oldest, so it is first-in-first-out; the piece would surface the name.)
pieces.walks_up_from: one sample entering an empty ring

pieces.what: The gain curve with W and R sliders, including R < 1 and W = 0, beside the spectrum of a sine pushed through it; hard knee vs quadratic knee heard and seen. Tests the bounded-Fourier claim.
pieces.walks_up_from: the straight unity line, no compression

pieces.what: The same buffer stretched to a second, holding a phrase (Retrospective Delay), to hear one primitive at two time scales.
